key_insight: Ammonia and hydrogen can separate under Uranus- and Neptune-like conditions, while remaining fully miscible in warmer sub-Neptune envelopes.
engineering_relevance: The predicted phase boundaries can improve planetary interior models by constraining ammonia rainout and its effects on composition, heat transport and structure.
method: Train machine-learning interatomic potentials on density functional theory calculations.
Run large-scale two-phase coexistence simulations across 500–4000 K and 0.1–100 GPa.
Map coexisting phase compositions and the critical curve separating miscibility from phase separation.
evidence_signal: The critical temperature rises from 500 K at 0.1 GPa to about 2000 K near 30 GPa, with no phase separation found at 3000 or 4000 K up to 100 GPa.
watch_item: Ammonia rainout is inferred from comparison with published planetary thermal profiles rather than directly observed.
paper_title: Ammonia-Hydrogen Phase Equilibria in Planetary Envelopes from First-Principles-Based Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
